record.paper_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
record.original_question: What is the full three-dimensional anisotropic structure of energy transfer across scales in kinetic plasma turbulence? This asks for a direct characterization of how the cascade is organized in three dimensions relative to the magnetic field and local turbulent structure.

evidence.quote: This includes answering fundamental questions about, for instance, ... (ii) the three-dimensional anisotropic structure of energy transfer across scales

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a magnetized collisionless plasma described by the Vlasov–Maxwell system in three spatial and three velocity dimensions, in a statistically homogeneous turbulent state with a mean magnetic field $\mathbf{B}_0$. In such a system energy injected at large (fluid) scales is transferred through a nonlinear cascade down to kinetic scales (ion and electron gyroradii and inertial lengths), where it is ultimately converted into particle heat.

Define the scale-dependent energy transfer rate using a generalized third-order (Yaglom-type / Kolmogorov-Hill) structure-function flux $\Pi(\boldsymbol{\ell})$, expressed as a function of the three-dimensional separation vector $\boldsymbol{\ell}$. Decompose $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ into:
- a component $\ell_\parallel$ parallel to the local mean magnetic field,
- a component $\ell_{\perp,1}$ perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}_0$ but aligned with the local fluctuation direction (e.g., the local perpendicular magnetic-field perturbation),
- a component $\ell_{\perp,2}$ perpendicular to both.

Problem. Determine the full three-dimensional anisotropic structure of the energy transfer rate $\Pi(\ell_\parallel,\ell_{\perp,1},\ell_{\perp,2})$ across the inertial, ion-kinetic, and sub-ion-kinetic ranges of a turbulent collisionless plasma. Specifically, characterize:
1. how the magnitude and direction of energy flux depend on the orientation of $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ with respect to both the local mean magnetic field and the local turbulent structure,
2. the scaling of $\Pi$ along each of the three axes as scales cross the ion gyroradius,
3. whether the cascade exhibits a single dominant transfer direction (e.g., predominantly perpendicular) or a non-trivial three-dimensional flux pattern, and
4. the relative role of the three symmetry axes in setting spectral slopes and dissipation channels.
artifact.status_search_result: The full three-dimensional anisotropic structure of the energy transfer in kinetic plasma turbulence remains an active research question. Recent work (e.g., a 2023 Phys. Rev. Lett. paper using MMS multipoint measurements to evaluate a 3D Yaglom flux, and 2024 A&A studies of ion-scale anisotropy) provides partial empirical characterizations but a complete theoretical/observational determination across inertial and kinetic ranges has not been achieved.

status_evidence.title: Three-Dimensional Energy Transfer in Space Plasma Turbulence from Multipoint Measurement
status_evidence.snippet: A novel multispacecraft technique applied to MMS data enables evaluation of the energy cascade rate from the full Yaglom equation; the method is inherently three-dimensional.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial progress: 3D energy flux can be measured but full anisotropic structure across all kinetic scales remains under investigation.

status_evidence.title: Anisotropy of plasma turbulence at ion scales
status_evidence.snippet: Study of anisotropy in plasma turbulence at ion scales using solar wind observations.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing characterization of anisotropy at ion scales indicates the question is not closed.

status_evidence.title: Scaling laws for the energy transfer in space plasma turbulence
status_evidence.snippet: Review of scaling laws for energy transfer in space plasma turbulence.
status_evidence.claim: Energy-transfer scaling laws in plasma turbulence remain a topic of active review.
